source_snapshot.procedure: On both in-band localhost and out-of-band lanplus paths, set disable with raw 0x3a 0x70 0x00, set enable with 0x3a 0x70 0x01 and get with 0x3a 0x71; the IB get line misspells ipmitool.
source_snapshot.criteria: Commands send without error and parameters display correctly.
source_snapshot.script: Literal state-changing OEM raw IPMI bytes; 10 attended/5 machine minutes; unique row/code/variant.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; recognizes state change/restore but incorrectly changes Get to raw 0x3a 0x70 and exposes password-style lanplus usage.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION/HIGH; requires firmware-specific OEM byte-map confirmation, read-before/write, response decoding, IB/OOB equivalence, secret-safe access and restoration.

old_problem: The Master lists opaque OEM bytes but supplies no firmware compatibility table, completion-code contract or response decoder for 0x71, so `parameters shown correctly` cannot be evaluated safely. DeepSeek further conflicts by using the state-changing 0x70 command as Get.
disposition_reason: ED-03/11/15/30 allow standard IPMI transport evidence but prohibit guessing OEM command semantics. The source bytes preserve intended coverage and the `iptmiool` spelling is an obvious non-semantic typo, yet exact BMC/BIOS firmware support, request/response layout, completion meanings and persistence/security effects remain unavailable. Without that authority a write may change another setting and raw success cannot prove a decoded state. The record therefore retains Pending while defining the complete IB/OOB state/restore matrix.
decision_basis: XLSX row 2219, same-row DeepSeek columns, GPT V2, historical record, unique identity and ED-01 through ED-30 were reviewed; actual next formal row Functionality 2220 / Wistron-BMC Sanity-00003-V002 / fe84b58dc647f4b1 was directly read from XLSX and its historical record.
Preserve Master semantics: set command is 0x3a/0x70 with data 00 or 01; Get is the separate 0x3a/0x71. Never issue 0x70 without its data byte as DeepSeek suggested.
Correct the executable tool typo `iptmiool` to ipmitool only in the review recipe; do not modify Master history.
Require OEM specification revision bound to exact SUT/BMC/BIOS firmware, supported channels/privileges and complete set/get byte layouts/decoders/completion codes.
Read and record initial decoded state before one approved transition, immediately read back, exercise IB and OOB separately as authorized, compare semantics, then restore and verify final state.
Use secret-safe authenticated transport; never put passwords in process listings/logs or disable evidence trust.
Stop on unsupported/unknown completion, unexpected response length/value, IB/OOB divergence, lost access or BMC/host fault without blind retry.
No IPMI query/write, credential use, state change, restore, retry, recovery or DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: Firmware-authorized OEM BIOS Debug Data IB/OOB set, get, decode and restore matrix
test_case.purpose: Verify BIOS Debug Data can be disabled and enabled through authorized in-band and out-of-band IPMI paths, read back through the OEM 0x71 command with identical decoded semantics, and restored to the approved final state without BMC/host side effects.
required_package: Exact SUT/BMC/BIOS firmware and OEM NetFn 0x3a command 0x70/0x71 specification
Set request, Get response byte layout, decoded 00/01 meanings and completion-code contract
IB/OOB channel, privilege, cipher and secret-safe authentication policy
Initial state, approved interface/state order, persistence scope and final state
Expected logging/performance/security effects, stop conditions and BMC/BIOS recovery
test_case.test_command: BLOCKED pending the firmware-bound OEM byte map and response decoder. Once signed, use protected credentials and the validated 0x3a/0x71 Get to record initial decoded state. For each authorized interface/state transition, issue exactly one 0x3a/0x70 00 or 01 Set, capture complete raw response/completion/exit/timestamp, immediately Get with 0x71 and decode, compare IB/OOB semantics, then restore and verify the signed final state. Preserve BMC/SEL/audit/host evidence and stop without retry on any anomaly.
test_case.expected_result: Every authorized IB/OOB Set returns an approved completion, the 0x71 response has the signed length/value and decodes to the requested state, both transports agree, no unexpected logging/performance/security or access fault occurs, and the final state is restored exactly.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: No PASS while the firmware-specific byte map, completion codes, decoder or final state is unapproved. After approval, unsupported/nonzero/unknown completion, wrong response length/value/decoded state, IB/OOB divergence, access or host/BMC fault, unexpected effect or failed restoration is FAIL. Shell exit or undecoded raw bytes alone cannot PASS.
safety_gate: Gate CLOSED until exact firmware/OEM byte specification, decoder, interface privileges, state order/final state and recovery are signed.
Read and record initial state before the first write; execute one transition at a time and verify before continuing.
Use protected credentials; no inline passwords, process/log exposure, insecure transport, 0x70-as-Get, unverified raw bytes or log clearing.
Stop on any unknown completion/value/length, transport divergence, lost access or fault; no blind retry.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash plus OEM specification revision and SUT/BMC/BIOS firmware identity
Initial decoded value, approved state/interface order and final-state authorization
Per-step IB/OOB request bytes and secret-redacted raw response/completion/exit/timestamps
Decoded 0x71 readback matching each requested state and cross-interface consistency
Restored final state, anomaly/recovery and engineer-verdict record
test_case.recovery: On unsupported completion, unexpected response, state divergence or access/fault anomaly, stop further raw writes and preserve evidence. Use the approved BMC/BIOS recovery path to restore the recorded initial/final state; do not guess inverse bytes, repeat the write or reset/power-cycle automatically.

source_conflict.reason: The unique Master row coherently uses 0x70 for Set and 0x71 for Get; the typo is unambiguous and DeepSeek's 0x70 Get is a review mismatch rather than a source conflict.

blocked.reason: The set/get/restore objective and literal source bytes are identifiable; missing firmware-bound OEM authority remains Engineering Decision Pending rather than an intrinsic static-review BLOCKED class.
